subject: Account bootstrapping & security hardening checklist — Atlas Health (private deploy)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Hayes <matthew.hayes@atlashealth.com>, Atlas Health Security <security@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Account bootstrapping & security hardening checklist — Atlas Health (private deploy)

Hi Matthew / Atlas Security team,

Thanks for the kickoff today — following up with a concise bootstrapping checklist so we can get the VPC/private deployment into a hardened, testable state. Attached are two templates: account_bootstrap_template.xlsx (project IDs, SA names, contact owners) and network_acl_template.txt (example ACL/SG rules).

High-level asks to unblock us this week:
- Confirm the GCP/Azure project IDs or on-prem environment name(s) you want Redwood to deploy into.
- Provide the service account naming convention + an initial public key for SSH jumpbox access (if required).
- Confirm KMS/HSM provider + key ARN(s) for model key wrapping (we support Cloud KMS or customer HSM via PKCS11).
- Supply expected egress / allowed outbound endpoints (we will add to the egress allowlist).
- Confirm whether audit logs must be routed to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and the target endpoints.

Proposed quick path: once we have the completed template and project IDs, Redwood will:
1) Provision service accounts and least-priv role bindings in a staging project.
2) Create initial networking constructs (subnets, NAT/egress rules) using the ACL template.
3) Wire KMS keys + verify envelope encryption.
4) Run a verification smoke test (token auth, sample inference, KV cache persistence).

Can you aim to return the filled template by EOD Friday? If any of these items are blocked on procurement or security review, flag them and we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: account_bootstrap_template.xlsx (spreadsheet), network_acl_template.txt (text)
From: Matthew Hayes <matthew.hayes@atlashealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Security <security@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account bootstrapping & security hardening checklist — Atlas Health (private deploy)

Sofia,

Appreciate the checklist and the template — useful. A couple quick asks from our side:
- Data residency: some patient-derived models must remain in our us-west region; can Redwood pin region for model artifacts and runtime?
- HSM: we're evaluating Thales HSM for key custody. Can you confirm Redwood's PKCS11 integration path and whether an on-prem HSM can be used for both model keys and signing artifacts?

We'll start filling the template. Security will attach a short KMS architecture diagram (sending separately). We'll aim to get project IDs and minimal answers by Friday, but procurement may slow HSM approvals — expect a 10 business day runway for that piece.

--
Matthew Hayes
Sr. Cloud Engineer, Atlas Health
matthew.hayes@atlashealth.com
Attachment: atlas-kms-arch.png
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Hayes <matthew.hayes@atlashealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account bootstrapping & security hardening checklist — Atlas Health (private deploy)

Thanks Matthew — quick replies inline and a proposed MAP (mutual action plan):

- Region pinning: yes, Redwood supports region pinning for model artifacts and runtime. We'll scope the storage/replication settings in the template.
- HSM support: we support Thales and AWS CloudHSM via PKCS11. For on-prem HSMs we typically run a small connector VM; we'll include integration notes in the onboarding playbook link below.

Proposed MAP and timeline:
1) Fri Aug 21: Atlas returns filled bootstrap template + project IDs (owner: Atlas).
2) Mon Aug 24: Redwood provisions staging resources + service accounts (owner: Redwood).
3) Wed Aug 26: Initial KMS integration test (owner: joint).
4) Fri Aug 28: Security hardening smoke test and telemetry routing verification.

Link to onboarding runbook / playbook: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0BzAtlas/bootstrapping-playbook

If Atlas is comfortable with the plan, we'll schedule a 30m sync Monday to walk through the service-account file and ACLs.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Account bootstrapping & security hardening checklist — Atlas Health (private deploy)

Hi Matthew / Team,

Quick status update after our env validation run this morning: thanks for the project IDs — we completed service account provisioning in the staging project and validated the base ACLs. Two items we flagged as blocking for the production cutover:

1) Egress allowlist: Atlas's list omitted our telemetry ingestion endpoints (splunk-ingest.redwood.com:443). Please confirm we can add this destination; without it, logs and traces won't reach your SIEM. Attached the CSV of outbound IPs we used (egress-allowlist.csv).

2) Firewall ports: the on-prem appliance currently blocks ephemeral high TCP ports (31000–32000) required for our continuous batching peer connections between inference nodes. Security will need to open that range between the subnet CIDRs of the Redwood runtime and the jump host.

Next steps we propose:
- Atlas Security to confirm allowance for splunk-ingest.redwood.com:443 and the ephemeral port range by Thu Aug 27.
- Once confirmed, Redwood will run a pre-cutover smoke which includes model load, KV persistence, and a sample inference vector test.

If anything here needs to be escalated to procurement or an architecture review, please flag now — we want to avoid surprises on cutover day.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Platform Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: egress-allowlist.csv
